clue.text: Pissed, covered in drink — move it!

indicators.note: something covered in a liquid sits wrapped inside it, so one word goes within the other

parts.note: to sup is to drink
pissed in the literal sense of urinated

explanation.surface: A drunk is told to hurry up and get going.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pissed' looks like British slang for drunk, but it is taken literally.
explanation.definitionFit: Telling someone to go faster is the same as urging them to move it, both being commands to hurry.

clue.text: (&11ac.) Liberal advocate would abandon one for right system of proportional representation

indicators.note: a liberal reading is loose and free, so the letters are not kept to their printed order
abandoning one thing in favour of another means swapping a letter out and a different one in

parts.note: taken as written
a is the article meaning one
R is the standard abbreviation for right

explanation.surface: A Liberal Democrat would gladly drop first-past-the-post for proportional representation.
explanation.walkthrough: Drop one A from the word advocate, add R, then shuffle. A card vote is the trade-union practice of casting votes weighted by membership size.
explanation.definitionFit: In a card vote each delegate's ballot counts in proportion to the members they represent, so voting power is weighted by numbers.

clue.text: Honest and up-front as a chairman of a bank is?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: open and legitimate, with nothing hidden

definitions.text: as a chairman of a bank is
definitions.meaning: second meaning, read literally: a chairman sits at the top, over the directors

explanation.surface: A wry question about whether bank chairmen are really honest.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the literal reading: the chairman ranks over the directors who form the bank's governing body.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes dealings conducted openly and legitimately, originally from card players keeping their hands visible on the table.

clue.text: see 9ac.
Brown cover-up appearing in the Eye

definitions.text: Brown cover-up appearing in the Eye

parts.words: Brown cover-up appearing in the Eye
parts.note: surface reading: a scandal concealed by Gordon Brown that Private Eye exposes
setter's reading: a brown condiment poured over food, which is also the title of the magazine's political column

explanation.surface: Private Eye reports on a scandal hushed up by Prime Minister Gordon Brown.
explanation.walkthrough: HP Sauce is a well-known British brown sauce, and also the name of Private Eye's long-running Westminster gossip column.
explanation.definitionFit: A famous bottled brown condiment poured over meals, sharing its name with a regular column printed in Private Eye.

clue.text: Unrestricted cuts at this establishment of fashion supported by vacuous royalty

parts.note: to fashion something is to carve or shape it

indicators.note: vacuous means empty, so the inside of the word is emptied out and only its ends remain

parts.note: only the first and last letters of royalty survive

explanation.surface: Fashionable royals back a fancy place where meat is sliced freely.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue, 'supported by' puts the second piece underneath the first.
explanation.definitionFit: A carvery is a restaurant where diners help themselves to as much roast meat as they like for a fixed price.

clue.text: Unpretty, ageing female gets sod all — told to shift and make way for Boris's top two

indicators.note: letters told to shift move about from their printed places into a new order

parts.note: sod all means nothing, which is zero
taken as written

parts.note: the opening two letters of Boris

explanation.walkthrough: Old boot is British slang, rude and dated, for an unattractive older woman.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is a disparaging slang term for a woman seen as elderly and unattractive.

clue.text: Relish genital area on getting mounted

parts.note: a coy euphemism: the lap is the area between waist and knees when seated

explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue, 'on' places the first piece above the second.
explanation.definitionFit: To lap something up is to enjoy it eagerly, so it is a phrasal verb for savouring with delight.

clue.text: (& 4dn.) Maybe Bush and Blair, fronting joint swindle, try a desperate charade to revive Labour?

definitions.text: a desperate charade to revive Labour

parts.note: both headed their countries' governments
the hip is a joint of the body
a con is a swindle
to try something is to test it

explanation.surface: Bush and Blair team up on a dodgy deal, while Labour stages a desperate show to recover.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fronting' puts the national heads before the joint. 'Maybe' marks Bush and Blair as examples.
explanation.definitionFit: A party electing a new head after defeat is often a staged contest meant to restore its fortunes, hence a cynical charade.

clue.text: Scottish female with a cruel twisted heart describing "Mythical Labour"

definitions.note: the answer is an adjective describing such a labour

indicators.note: a heart sits at the centre of a body, so these letters go in the middle of the other word

parts.note: hen is a Scottish form of address to a woman

indicators.note: something twisted is bent out of shape, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A cruel-hearted Scotswoman writes about the Labour Party's legendary past.
explanation.walkthrough: The capital in Labour sends one to the political party, but it means a task, as in the twelve labours of Hercules.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective means needing enormous strength or effort, named after the Greek hero who performed twelve legendary tasks.

taken as written

explanation.walkthrough: Ant McPartlin and Declan Donnelly present popular British TV shows as Ant and Dec.

clue.text: Superb, unlikely Republican leader kicked out Bush

clue.text: Plus type of sex chromosome associated with Brand (prone to ranting for Labour candidate)

clue.text: Abuse dick one last month

clue.text: Complaint from Dicky on receiving head
